record.paper_title: On open problems in polling systems
record.context_brief: Renewal-arrival polling systems with large deterministic switch-over times
record.original_question: Consider a cyclic polling system with finitely many queues, deterministic switch-over times between successive queues, and general renewal arrival processes at the queues. The source conjectures that, when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity, the polling system converges to a deterministic cyclic system. Provide a rigorous proof of that conjecture.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2. A cyclic polling system with general (renewal) arrival processes converges to a deterministic cyclic system when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity.

Open problem 2. Provide a rigourous proof of Conjecture 4.2, which states that a cyclic polling system with general (renewal) arrival processes converges to a deterministic cyclic system when the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cyclic polling system defined as follows. There are N ≥ 2 queues Q_1, ..., Q_N served by a single server that visits them in the cyclic order Q_1 → Q_2 → ... → Q_N → Q_1 → .... Customers arrive at queue Q_i according to an independent renewal process with generic inter-arrival time A_i (with finite mean 1/λ_i) and require independent service times with generic distribution B_i (finite mean). Between completing service at Q_i and starting service at Q_{i+1}, the server incurs a deterministic switch-over time s_i ≥ 0. Within each queue, the server uses a fixed work-conserving service discipline (e.g., exhaustive or gated). Assume the total load ρ = Σ_i λ_i E[B_i] < 1 so that the system is stable.

Let S = Σ_i s_i denote the total switch-over time per cycle, and consider the family of such polling systems indexed by S, where the individual switch-over times s_i are scaled so that S → ∞ (e.g., s_i = α_i S for fixed positive weights α_i summing to 1). Let "the deterministic cyclic system" denote the idealized system in which arrivals at each queue occur at deterministic equidistant epochs with rate λ_i and service times equal to their means E[B_i], with the same switch-over structure.

Prove rigorously that, as S → ∞, the stochastic cyclic polling system with general renewal arrivals converges (in an appropriate distributional sense, e.g., for the joint stationary distribution of scaled queue lengths and waiting times at polling instants) to the corresponding deterministic cyclic system.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a clearly identifiable rigorous proof of the specific conjecture that a cyclic polling system with general renewal arrivals converges to a deterministic cyclic system as the deterministic switch-over times tend to infinity. Related work exists on heavy-traffic limits and on polling systems with renewal arrivals and nonzero switch-over times, but no direct resolution of this large-switch-over-time limit conjecture was found.

status_evidence.title: A note on polling models with renewal arrivals and nonzero switch-over times
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses polling models with renewal arrivals and nonzero switch-over times but addresses waiting-time approximations rather than the large-switch-over-time limit.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on renewal arrivals with switch-over times exists but does not directly prove the stated limit conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Polling systems with periodic server routing in heavy traffic: renewal arrivals
status_evidence.snippet: Studies heavy-traffic limits with renewal arrivals.
status_evidence.claim: Existing rigorous limit results for polling systems with renewal arrivals concern heavy-traffic, not large switch-over times.
